title: Securing Internal Microservice Communication
business: Internal microservices architectures where service-to-service traffic traverses shared network infrastructure.
problem: Unencrypted traffic between internal services is vulnerable to eavesdropping and tampering by unauthorized actors with access to the internal network fabric.
solution: Implementing TLS 1.3 provides a secure channel between communicating peers, ensuring confidentiality and integrity of data in transit through robust handshake and record protocols.
steps: Negotiate cryptographic parameters using the TLS 1.3 handshake protocol to establish shared keying material.
Authenticate the server using asymmetric cryptography or pre-shared keys to verify identity.
Utilize the record protocol to independently protect traffic records using established traffic keys.
Apply record padding to obscure data lengths and mitigate potential traffic analysis.
outcome: A hardened communication environment where data remains confidential and tamper-evident even if the underlying network is compromised.
limitation: TLS 1.3 does not hide the length of the data it transmits, which can potentially be used for traffic analysis; this can be checked by monitoring record sizes and packet timing patterns.
